title: Temp: inference-batching-experiments-wip
content:
Quick dump of notes from ad-hoc experiments in the infra lab. This is messy — saved here so I don't lose commands and weird results.

Summary:
- Trying to characterize latency vs throughput behavior for micro-batching heuristics on rtx-4k nodes.
- Observed odd spikes when batch_size ~ 16 and seq_len skew > 512. Might be scheduler interaction or an alignment bug in kernel selection.

Commands run (approx):
- run_bench --model redwood-3b --quant q4_0 --batch 8 --seq 256 --repeat 30
- run_bench --model redwood-3b --quant q4_0 --batch 16 --seq 1024 --p30
- stress_streamer --clients 50 --burst 200 --p95

Raw observations:
- batch=8 seq=256 stable p95=42ms but p99=120ms occasionally
- batch=16 seq=1024 p95 drops to 60ms (higher throughput) but every ~200s p99 jumps to 420ms for ~4s
- toggling kv_cache off reduces p99 jumps but increases avg token CPU

Hypotheses:
1) KV cache eviction/rehydration racing with scheduler thread (timing-sensitive). Look for KV cache lock stats.
2) When sequence length distribution is heavy-tailed, model runtime picks a different kernel that degrades under certain memory alignment. Need to log chosen kernel names.
3) CUDA memory fragmentation at sustained throughput — try larger allocation pools or bump cudamalloc retry thresholds.

Quick TODOs/next steps:
- Add explicit kernel_name to bench output (kernel: <name>) — patch bencher and run small 2h sweep (Aisha)
- Capture nvprof/perf counters around p99 spikes and correlate with scheduler metrics (Marcus)
- Run same batch/seq combos with quant=q8_0 to see if quantization changes pattern (Liam)
- Try prewarm routine that touches all KV shards before burst to see if rehydration cost hides (experiment: prewarm=true)

Notes / random:
- Saw an unrelated Docker image tag mismatch (inference:latest vs inference:202602) on one node, fixed by pulling explicit tag. Keep nodes pegged to tag during experiments.
- Logged a weird HTTP 499 on the measurement collector; double-check collector ingress and reverse-proxy timeouts.

Scratch results (CSV-ish):
case, batch, seq, p95_ms, p99_ms, notes
A,8,256,42,120,stable
B,16,1024,60,420,p99 spikes
C,16,1024,65,110,kv_cache_off

WIP decisions:
- No rollout changes yet. This stays internal until we have repro and root cause.

If anyone pulls this file, add your short notes below and timestamp so we can iterate.

-- Liam
